args.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

In src/ingest/parser.ts, parseStatement splits the input text by newline and pops the last line if it is empty:
  const lines = text.split("\n");
  if (lines.length > 0 && lines[lines.length - 1] === "") lines.pop();

However, when a CSV file ends with an empty line (or multiple consecutive newlines), splitting by "\n" on a string ending with "\n" leaves an empty string at the very end of the lines array, which gets popped. If there are multiple trailing newlines (e.g., a file ending with "\r\n" where splitting by "\n" leaves an empty string containing "\r", or consecutive empty trailing lines), or if the bookkeeping software's export adds an empty line followed by a carriage return or another blank line, the popped line is not the empty line causing the failure, or lines still contains an empty string or whitespace-only line at the end that is processed as a data row. Specifically, if the last line has a carriage return ('\r') or whitespace, lines[lines.length - 1] === "" check fails because the last element is "\r" or " ", so it is not popped and gets processed as a row, resulting in a 'Malformed row' error.
